title.en: Practical 2: Thickness of an iron nail (screw gauge)

text.en: A screw gauge can measure even a hair-thin difference.

The aim is to find the thickness of an iron nail using a screw gauge. The apparatus is the screw gauge and the nail.
The least count of the screw gauge is 0.01 mm. First find the zero error when the two faces touch each other. Then place the nail between the faces and note the pitch scale reading (PSR) and head scale coincidence (HSC), and repeat with other parts of the nail.
Thickness t = PSR + (HSC x LC) +/- zero correction. For a positive zero error of 5 points subtract 5 points; for a negative error of 95 points add 5 points (100 - 95). Tabulate and average the readings.
